summary: Exhaustive packet-bound Q4 review of task commit bb2e042c45873da3f3d78836d915ddb6446debf2 finds five blocking contract-alignment defects. The verifier materially binds undocumented private src.* Python APIs; movement/item/warehouse acceptance policy is only partially covered; several documented reconciliation/publication safety cases are untested; successful rejected-movement durability is not verified through checkpoint/restart behavior; and the public preflight/audit/archive operator contract retains material coverage holes. Instruction shape and the instruction-versus-docs boundary are otherwise acceptable, and the second adversarial omission sweep is complete.

evidence.observation: Edition 3 disallows unstated grading requirements and requires tasks to be fully specified and behaviorally testable; instruction.md may contain up to 20 concise functional bullets.
Q4 is a cold packet-bound post-freeze review and must be exhaustive rather than stop at the first reason for REVISE.
Q4 is exact-task-commit bound, findings must be evidence-bound, and current reviewer evidence must respect packet isolation.
Q4 must build both requirement-to-test and test-to-requirement matrices, inspect F2P/P2P and public/private boundaries, and treats material phantom tests or untested requirements as REVISE.
Q4 must identify phantom implementation choices/private return-value contracts, inspect public output interfaces and operator workflows, and perform a second adversarial omission sweep.
Material functional and operational requirements belong in the work request; technical docs may define protocol/API/CLI/state details but must not become a second prompt or repair map.

The 16-bullet work request explicitly defines movement shape, item/warehouse authority, durability/replay, reconciliation/detail safety, publication, preflight, audit and archive obligations and delegates detailed runtime semantics to runtime-contract.md.

The solver-visible contract declares the public executable/SQLite/report operational interface, exact packed/layout/durability/reconciliation/publication/CLI semantics, and preflight/audit/archive responsibilities.
The solver-visible schema exposes items.active, items.max_unit_cost, items.quantity_precision, warehouses.active and generation-scoped operational tables/constraints.
The documented public runtime surface is the equiv-eval executable and its init-db, describe-layout, identity, run, preflight, audit and archive command interfaces.
The complete 40-test verifier was inspected. It combines public CLI/state checks with extensive direct imports and calls into undocumented src.* implementation APIs.

Used only for the packet-permitted classification purpose: 30 tests are classified F2P and 10 P2P. Requirement ownership/mapping in this review was rebuilt independently from solver-visible contracts and test bodies.

findings.criterion: Verifier behavior -> discoverable solver-visible contract; no phantom private implementation/API contract.
findings.why_it_matters: Many substantive tests directly require exact undocumented internal symbols and signatures such as src.comp3.PackedSpec/pack/unpack, src.layout.Field/Layout/resolve_offsets/active_occurs, src.generation/checkpoint helpers, src.accounting helpers, src.policy validators, src.publication.atomic_publish, src.reconciliation.reconcile and src.pipeline.process. The solver-visible contract instead defines the public equiv-eval/SQLite/report behavior and does not declare these Python APIs stable. A conforming implementation that preserves the documented observable behavior while refactoring those internals can therefore fail grading.
findings.minimal_remediation: Move behavior that is externally observable to CLI/database/report/publication scenarios. Retain a direct internal assertion only where that Python API is itself intentionally made a stable, naturally solver-visible contract; do not expose hidden test topology or an implementation recipe merely to legitimize the current tests.
findings.regression_risk: Replacing fine-grained unit checks with black-box checks can reduce diagnostic precision; preserve equivalent negative and preservation scenarios at the documented public/state boundary.

findings.criterion: Material solver-visible movement/item/warehouse acceptance requirements -> meaningful verifier coverage.
evidence_refs: GitHub code search within cobol-comp3-python-equiv/tests for max_unit_cost, quantity_precision, ITEM_UNKNOWN, WAREHOUSE_UNKNOWN, UNIT_COST_LIMIT, QUANTITY_PRECISION, RECEIPT_SOURCE and ISSUE_DESTINATION
findings.why_it_matters: The work request makes the movement-shape matrix and the solver-visible item/warehouse fields part of the acceptance contract. Current tests cover zero quantity, same-warehouse transfer, reason/type compatibility, inactive item and inactive warehouse, but they do not distinguish implementations that ignore items.max_unit_cost or items.quantity_precision, accept an unknown item or warehouse, or omit several required source/destination shape rules such as receipt-with-source and issue-with-destination. These are movement acceptance/rejection semantics, so plausible incorrect implementations can pass.
findings.minimal_remediation: Add public-behavior scenarios that exercise each missing policy family without coupling to private validator functions. Preserve the stated authority model: items use the solver-visible active/max-unit-cost/quantity-precision fields, warehouses use existence plus active status only, and no hidden capability switch is introduced.
findings.regression_risk: New cases can accidentally turn non-stable internal validation codes into public requirements or reintroduce warehouse capability switches that the instruction expressly excludes.

findings.criterion: Reconciliation/detail/publication safety requirements -> complete behavioral coverage.
findings.why_it_matters: The suite meaningfully covers all six legacy controls/tolerances, duplicate movement identities, orphan effects, unbalanced transfers, accepted-with-no-effect publication blocking, negative quantity, reconciliation gating, atomic publication, same-generation idempotency and corrupt published content. It does not exercise the separate documented detailed-settlement prohibition on duplicate effects of the same effect kind for one movement, the inventory-value floor below -0.01 with non-negative quantity, or the documented conflicting-existing-publication case distinct from corruption. Implementations omitting those safety checks remain verifier-green.
findings.minimal_remediation: Add representation-neutral state perturbations for duplicate same-kind effects and the negative-value threshold, and a same-target conflicting-generation/publication scenario. Assert only the documented safety/publication outcomes, not incidental manifest filenames, serialization or promotion primitives.
findings.regression_risk: Over-specific publication fixtures can accidentally make serialization/layout or an internal promotion mechanism part of the grading contract.

findings.criterion: Rejected-movement durability/replay contract -> meaningful positive and failure-path coverage.
findings.why_it_matters: The rejected-transaction fault-injection test proves rollback when the REJECT journal insertion fails, and successful reject-code tests prove reject persistence. They do not verify that a successfully rejected movement also advances the checkpoint atomically, records the applicable processed status, and is skipped on restart. A runtime can persist the reject/event but omit the durable checkpoint, then reprocess the same rejected record after restart, while satisfying the current verifier.
findings.minimal_remediation: Add a successful rejected-record durability scenario that checks the documented checkpoint fingerprint/last-sequence advance and applicable processed state, then reruns/resumes and proves the rejected movement is not duplicated. Keep decode cases consistent with the contract's 'processed-row status when applicable' qualification.
findings.regression_risk: A blanket processed-row assertion for malformed records could overstate the documented 'when applicable' rule; separate decodable policy rejects from boundary-indeterminate decode rejects.

findings.criterion: Stable public preflight/audit/archive operator contracts -> meaningful, representation-neutral verifier coverage.
findings.why_it_matters: The operator workflow tests are broad but leave material distinctions unprobed. Preflight proves an actually empty catalog fails, not that a non-empty catalog with zero active items/warehouses fails, so a row-count-only catalog check can pass. Audit perturbations mostly assert only overall passed=false (or a changed payload), not that the documented replay/recovery, checkpoint, accounting, reconciliation, inventory, quarantine, journal, registry, metric and settlement health is actually exposed in the public result. Archive is exercised only against healthy report/publication inputs; publication corruption is tested against audit and restored before archive, so an archive implementation that packages evidence without first verifying the live report/publication contract can pass. These gaps affect documented public operator behavior and archive integrity, so this MEDIUM finding is blocking under Q4 materiality.
findings.minimal_remediation: Add an all-inactive-but-nonempty catalog preflight case; verify audit semantically exposes each documented health family without freezing incidental JSON field names/serialization; and invoke archive against a semantically corrupt report/publication set and require refusal/no verified archive or archive event.
findings.regression_risk: Operator tests must remain representation-neutral: do not manufacture a new exact JSON schema or archive file naming contract that solver-visible material does not define.

REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.REQUIREMENT: ODO bounds, REDEFINES storage/offset behavior and determinable versus indeterminate malformed-record boundaries.
REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.NOTES: Semantic cases are present; direct internal API binding is separately a reverse-contract defect.

REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.REQUIREMENT: Generation identity binds source SHA-256, layout SHA-256 and business date; checkpoint fingerprint mismatch cannot resume; resume starts at last durable sequence + 1.

REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.REQUIREMENT: Current-generation replay does not reapply inventory effects; same movement identity in another generation is not itself a duplicate.
REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.NOTES: Replay and cross-generation ownership are both exercised.

REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.REQUIREMENT: Accepted movement processed row, effects, positions, journal and checkpoint commit atomically.
REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.NOTES: Fault injection plus restart/state assertions distinguish partial accepted commits.

REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.REQUIREMENT: Rejected movement reject row, applicable processed status, journal and checkpoint commit atomically and are durable across restart.
REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.NOTES: Rollback and reject persistence are covered; successful reject checkpoint/applicable processed state and restart skip are not. See Q4-004.

REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.REQUIREMENT: Stable reject codes DECODE, TRANSFORM, ACCOUNTING, QUANTITY, TRANSFER_LOOP, ITEM_INACTIVE and WAREHOUSE_INACTIVE persist in operational reject evidence; human wording is not stable.
REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.NOTES: Each documented stable code family is observed.

REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.REQUIREMENT: Movement quantity/source/destination shape and reason/type compatibility are enforced before acceptance.
REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.NOTES: Reason matrix, zero quantity and transfer loop are covered; several required source/destination invalid shapes are not. See Q4-002.

REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.REQUIREMENT: Item must exist and item policy uses items.active, items.max_unit_cost and items.quantity_precision.
REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.NOTES: Active status is covered; unknown item, max_unit_cost and quantity_precision are not. See Q4-002.

REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.REQUIREMENT: Every referenced warehouse must exist and have warehouses.active=1; no additional solver-visible receipt/issue/transfer capability switch is authoritative.
REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.NOTES: Active warehouse is covered; missing warehouse is not independently exercised. See Q4-002.

REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.REQUIREMENT: Available quantity and weighted source valuation govern inventory effects; resulting inventory quantity is non-negative.
REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.NOTES: Available quantity, weighted issue valuation, zero-net transfer valuation and negative quantity are distinguished.

REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.REQUIREMENT: All six legacy controls are compared independently with count tolerance 0, quantity tolerance 0.0001 and value tolerance 0.01.
REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.NOTES: Each control is independently mismatched and tolerance boundaries are exercised.

REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.REQUIREMENT: Safety reconciliation enforces zero duplicate movement identities, orphan effects and unbalanced transfer pairs.
REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.NOTES: Unbalanced transfer plus permissive duplicate/orphan state are exercised.

REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.REQUIREMENT: Detailed settlement requires at least one effect per accepted movement, no duplicate same-kind effects for one movement, non-negative position quantity and value >= -0.01.
REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.NOTES: Missing-effect and negative-quantity cases are covered; duplicate same-kind effect and isolated value-floor violation are not. See Q4-003.

REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.REQUIREMENT: Publication is reconciliation/detail gated, atomically visible, independently verifiable, idempotent only for a valid same generation, and rejects corrupt/conflicting existing publication.
REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.NOTES: Gate, atomic visibility, integrity and corrupt-existing cases are covered; a distinct conflicting existing generation/manifest case is absent. See Q4-003.

REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.REQUIREMENT: Preflight consumes real source/layout, schema health, catalog, input integrity, 15,000-row historical baseline, batch-window/authorization safety and recovery state; zero active catalog or unsafe recovery fails.
REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.NOTES: Many perturbations exist, but the active-catalog obligation is only tested by deleting all rows rather than leaving rows present but all inactive. See Q4-005.

REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.REQUIREMENT: Audit exposes replay/recovery, checkpoint, accounting/control/reconciliation, inventory, quarantine, journal, registry, metric and settlement health for the generation.
REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.NOTES: Perturbations drive overall pass/fail, but the public result is not checked for semantic exposure of each documented health family. See Q4-005.

REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.REQUIREMENT: Archive verifies report/publication contracts, exports controls/deltas, binds lineage/integrity, creates a verified archive, records registry/journal evidence, reports positive retention for report/publication/audit/quarantine, and does not mutate live report/publication.
REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.NOTES: Positive archive evidence/retention/non-mutation is strong; archive is not invoked against corrupt report/publication inputs to prove verification refusal. See Q4-005.

REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.REQUIREMENT: SQLite state preserves generation-scoped movement identity/sequence and reject sequence ownership while allowing the same movement id in another generation; report/publication state remains compatible with solver-visible contracts.
REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.NOTES: Generation/reject uniqueness and representative public state/report compatibility are asserted.

REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.REQUIREMENT: Successful CLI commands emit one JSON object on stdout with exit 0; completed failed checks return 2 with passed=false; runtime/input errors emit one JSON error object on stderr and return 2.
REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.NOTES: Success, completed-check failure and input/runtime error paths are exercised.
